acceptance: Each proposal has executable scenarios: the cap and step-back keep every open finding; delta-first follow-ups still count unchanged hunks for coverage; pre-existing advisory applies only when the diff agrees; Critical/High never become advisory; the intent block cannot inject instructions; the guidance file is read from the base only and refused when oversized.
The eval corpus seeds each session incident with an expected finding: the substitute capacity bypass, the test weakenings on #3962, and the stdlib patching on #3962. The CI subset is deterministic.
Released as v0.2.5 through Theseus's own review gate, after independent review, with assets verified.
Re-measured 4 weeks after the BenchBox re-lock with the same method. Targets: one-round pass ≥75%, PRs needing 5+ rounds ≤2%, already-seen late findings ≤25%, incomplete ≤5%.
description:
Reviews here are strict but slow to converge. Baseline on 280 merged BenchBox PRs (2026-10-28 to 11-07):
- 59.3% pass in one round;
- 10.0% need 5 or more rounds;
- 51% of late findings are on code already reviewed;
- 15.6% of attempts end absent-incomplete.
The plan is in local://review-practice-integration-plan.md (proposals P1, P2, P3, P5, P6). Owner decisions 2026-11-07:
- D1: `protocol.max_finding_rounds: 4`.
- D2: at the cap, one full-scope step-back re-review that keeps finding ids and never drops an open defect. Later rounds stage a since-last-review delta first. Findings name the bug class.
- D3: a consumer `review_guidance` file, trusted, read from the base only, and bounded. Move the BenchBox-specific prose out of the OSS templates (standard.md).
- D4: `origin: pre-existing` is honoured only when the model says so AND the trusted diff adds no line there. Medium/Low pre-existing findings are advisory; Critical/High always block.
- D5: every other severity still blocks.
- D8: PR title, body and tracker intent go into the brief as fenced, untrusted data.
- D9: an incident → eval corpus with `tools/review_eval.py`. Template, model or guidance changes must not lower the score. A deterministic subset runs in CI; a live run weekly.
- D12: one release.
Second-family panel deferred (D6).
